THE_QUESTION: Can the 58 binary office/zip files in the share be read into text? This matters because no local converter, ffmpeg, or office install is permitted, and because 3 of the 5 bonus courses carry these as their written register.

what_does_MEGA_declare.finding: The `title` attribute is '<type> <size> <name>' for MEDIA (e.g. 'MPEG Audio 258 MB call.mp3') but only '<size> <name>' for office documents (e.g. '174 KB 4. 7-Figure Sales Letter.docx').
what_does_MEGA_declare.consequence: The declared MIME type is NOT recoverable from the listing for .docx/.pptx/.xlsx. An earlier probe that split the title on the first space and reported the leading token as a 'type' was reporting the SIZE. The file EXTENSION is the only type signal available without fetching.
what_does_MEGA_declare.class: harness_artefact — the probe read the wrong field, the data was never absent.

can_we_read_them.method: SYNTHETIC round-trip. Build a minimal .docx / .xlsx / .pptx, then read it back with the Python STANDARD LIBRARY ONLY (zipfile + xml.etree.ElementTree). No third-party library, no converter, no office install.
can_we_read_them.why_synthetic_is_correct_here: The question is a CAPABILITY question - 'can a ZIP+XML container be parsed without conversion tools' - not a corpus question. Answering it on synthetic files answers it fully, and keeps the corpus read-only with zero bytes fetched. Nothing about the answer depends on which particular .docx it is.
can_we_read_them.VERDICT: EXTRACTABLE. .docx / .xlsx / .pptx are ZIP containers of XML. zipfile + ElementTree recover paragraphs, shared strings and slide text with the standard library alone.
can_we_read_them.consequence_for_the_build: The 57 office files (0.33 GB combined) are in scope for the written register with NO new dependency and NO conversion step. This removes a capability risk that had been sitting as an open question since the first census.

STILL_NOT_PROVEN: That the corpus files are genuinely OOXML rather than, say, legacy .doc or renamed binaries. The EXTENSION says .docx/.pptx/.xlsx and MEGA's own type column for these carries no type prefix, so this is unconfirmed until one is actually fetched. The probe path is unaffected: zipfile.is_zipfile() is a one-line check at fetch time, and a non-zip file is reported as such rather than silently yielding empty text.
